processes.name: EFT donations
processes.purpose: Find, enter and tie out electronic gifts (DAFs, employer matches, bill pay and other EFTs) in Salesforce. Gifts are entered daily as they arrive; the EFT and Misc batches are processed every Thursday, covering Friday–Thursday. The EFT batch holds most DAF and matching gifts; the Misc batch holds bill pay, stock and one-off electronic gifts.

sections.title: Daily: find and enter new gifts

steps.text:
Check the bank for incoming wires: log in to online banking, open the Incoming Wires account and pick the date range. Match each bank display name to the EFT source table below for its portal, login and email pattern (bank names are often cut short).
Not entered in the EFT batch: Amazon royalties (not a gift), NCF and Fidelity (imported, see below), iPay Solutions and Allied Payment (Misc batch), Overflow stock gifts (Misc batch), Patreon (API) and other one-offs.

Wire from a company name that isn’t in the table? Check Bonterra (Cybergrants) → FrontDoor first: many employer matches arrive with just the company name. Use the finance@ login in Bitwarden (Shared-Financial), or clara@ if the gift isn’t found. If it isn’t in Cybergrants, investigate.

Check the Finance inbox for the matching gift emails. If the EFT isn’t in the bank yet, label the email Awaiting (or mark it unread). Leave every labelled email in the inbox until the batch is tied out.

Get the donor details. Portal gifts: log in with Bitwarden (Shared-Financial), complete any 2FA, go to the disbursements/payments/grants page and screenshot or download the gift(s). Email-only gifts: take them from the email body or attachment. Fidelity secure email: see the Fidelity steps.

Create the Salesforce batch: Gift Entry → Create New Batch → “Check/NCF Entry/Next Action” template → Next. Name it for the day you’ll process it (“6.11.2026 EFTs”, or “6.11.2026 Misc” for bill pay and one-off electronic gifts) → Next.
Defaults: Contact1; Record Type Donation; Payment Method Wire (Misc batch: Check for bill pay, PayPal for PayPal, Wire for anything by wire/ACH). Save.

Enter each gift. Switch to Account1 if the donor is an organization, then link the existing contact or account: search individuals by last name (or address/email if the name is common), organizations and giving funds in the Organization box. Always click “Show more results for” to check the details or create a new record. With duplicates, use the one with more contact information or more donations.
Record Type: Matching Donation for a company match (and fill Matching Gift Account). Amount = the total; Close Date = date received; Donor Advised = the DAF name (always, in the EFT batch).
Then relabel the email Entered. Don’t archive it yet.

Save the support: an Excel export, or a screenshot that shows every donor detail and the amount. Name it source + amount (“ren 100”, “cybergrants 250”) and file it in Google Drive → Finance Documents → EFT → [Thursday processing date] folder (create it if needed, e.g. “6.11.2026 EFTs”).

sections.title: Thursdays: tie out and process the batches

steps.text: In Salesforce, note the total of the open EFT batch.

Export the Incoming Wires CSV from online banking for the batch period (usually Friday–Thursday, 5 business days). Strike out every line that isn’t in the EFT batch: Amazon royalties, NCF, Fidelity, iPay Solutions, Allied Payment, Overflow, Patreon and other one-offs.
Sum the remaining lines: the total should match the EFT batch. If it doesn’t, go through the batch and the CSV line by line to find the difference before processing.
Totals match: process the EFT batch in Salesforce and archive the emails labelled Entered for this batch.
Do the same for the Misc batch, summing only its lines in the CSV (bill pay, Overflow stock and other one-off electronic gifts). Once it ties, process it and archive its Entered emails.

sections.title: Chariot: move the funds before the EFT arrives

steps.text: Watch the Finance inbox for a Chariot gift notification from Daffy, GiveClear or Groundswell (all route through Chariot). Enter the gift in the EFT batch from the email and label it Entered.

Once a week (with the Thursday run, or as gifts build up), log in to the Chariot portal (Bitwarden, Shared-Financial; Google Authenticator) and click “Move funds”. Your disbursement is what triggers the wire, so don’t wait for it.
The EFT shows in the bank the next business day: confirm the amount matches what was entered in Salesforce.

sections.title: NCF: import instead of entering by hand

steps.text: The NCF eGrants email arrives about 2 business days before the EFT. Log in to the NCF Charity Portal (Bitwarden, Shared-Financial; no 2FA), choose “Last 30 days” and Export to Excel. Label the email Imported / To Be Imported. NCF gifts never go in the EFT batch.

In the NCF folder, copy “NCF Import - Template with Dup Matching” into dated & cloned templates and name it for the donation dates. Paste the gifts not yet entered (no headers) into the “Raw File - NCF” tab, and update the SF Reference IDs as needed (see the how-to video).

When every reference ID is filled in, go to the “Dup match - Template for NPSP Importer Tool” tab → File → Download CSV. Delete ALL rows below the last row of patron data first, or they import too and Michelle has to delete them. Save the file.

Salesforce → NPSP Data Imports → Import. Match the first-page settings to the screenshot in the guide, upload the CSV, map the Donation DAF field to “Donation DAF” and leave the last 2 columns unmapped. Continue → Start Import → Import All Data Records → check the fields on the final screen against the guide → Begin Data Import Process. Archive the email once the import is confirmed.

sections.title: Fidelity: import instead of entering by hand

steps.text: The FIDELITYSECURE email arrives about 1 business day before the EFT. Open it with the access code to get the donor details, and label it Imported / To Be Imported. Fidelity gifts never go in the EFT batch.

In the Fidelity folder, copy “Fidelity Import - Template with Dup Matching” into dated & cloned templates, named for the donation dates. Paste the gifts (no headers) from the raw file into the “Raw File - Fidelity” tab. Remove any email addresses from the address columns, combine unit/apartment numbers into “Acknowledgement Address Line 1”, and update the SF Reference IDs (see the how-to video).
“Dup match - Template for NPSP Importer Tool” tab → File → Download CSV, after deleting ALL rows below the last row of patron data. Save the file.
Import it through NPSP Data Imports exactly as for NCF (map Donation DAF, leave the last 2 columns unmapped, Begin Data Import Process). Archive the emails once the import is confirmed.
Patreon gift disbursements reach Salesforce through the API. Nothing to enter, and they’re struck out of the Thursday tie-out.

processes.name: Check gifts: mail, deposit and Salesforce
processes.purpose: Open and sort the mail, deposit the checks in Cass, scan the support and notes, and enter every check as a gift in Salesforce. The Salesforce batch must match the deposit to the cent.

steps.text: Pick up mail from the mailroom downstairs and from the Post Office (1020 SE 7th Ave, Portland, OR, PO Box 14278).

As you open it, check: is it for BibleProject, or for Imago or someone else? Which month is the donation for? Is it an individual’s check, a donor advised fund (DAF) or a qualified charitable distribution (QCD)? If it isn’t a donation, what is it and who should get it? Keep everything in order so mistakes are easy to trace later.

Sort into piles: Donations (a separate pile per month), Deposit Support (information about a check: the grant or person it came from), Deposit Notes (notes from donors, often encouragement or thanks) and Other (mail for specific people or departments).
2 or 3 times a year, Omaha Community Charity Foundation emails a check: print it, cut it and deposit it like any other. If you can’t print, try sending it to Cass to deposit.

In the Deposit Count Google Sheet, duplicate the most recent tab (right-click → Duplicate), rename it to the deposit date and delete the old entries. Add the deposit date in the green cell at the bottom.

Carry over the addition formula: on the previous tab, screenshot rows 1–3 across to column D (one month) or column F (two months), paste it into the new tab, and enter each check amount under the $ sign.

Log in to Cass Deposit (link below; the login and security answers are in LastPass). At the top left, deposit into the Operating Account with the Deposit Control Amount = the deposit total. Different months (e.g. December and January) are separate deposits.

Scan all the checks (open the WebScan app if the scanner needs connecting). Once the deposit matches the control amount, save “Deposit Image: Front Only” as deposit date + month + DepositImageFrontOnly, e.g. “1.26.23 January DepositImageFrontOnly”.

sections.title: Scan support, notes and other mail

steps.text: Plug in the Epson scanner. Scan Deposit Support (split by month if there’s more than one) as “1.26.23 Deposit Support”, and Deposit Notes (encouragement, address changes) as “1.26.23 Deposit Notes”.
Scan each piece of Other mail on its own so it can be sent on, named for what it is (e.g. “Library of Congress”).

sections.title: Enter the check gifts in Salesforce

steps.text: Open Salesforce → the 9 dots at the top left → search “Gift Entry” → New Batch (top right) → Check/NCF Entry → Next.

Batch Name = deposit date + “Deposit” (e.g. “1/26/2023 Deposit”). With two months, make one batch each: “1/26/2023 December Deposit” and “1/26/2023 January Deposit”. Expected Total Batch Amount = the deposit total. Next → set the default to Contact 1 → Save.

For each check: Contact1 for an individual, Account1 for an organization (e.g. Northwest Naturals). Link the existing contact or account. Opportunity Amount = the check total; Close Date = the date of the check. Never fill both Contact and Account: an affiliate account fills in automatically for a contact.

When it applies, fill Donor Advised (a gift through a fund; the support usually mentions a grant) or Qualified Charitable Donation Account (from an investment account: IRA, principal account…). Never both. See the DAF vs. QCD list below.
Make sure the total entered equals the deposit control amount, and take a screenshot of the matching totals.

Upload Deposit Notes and Deposit Support to the deposit folder in Google Drive (link below), and post in the Patron Slack channel that they’re ready. Call out anything that needs attention, like a tax receipt request or a gift in memory of someone who has died.
A check donation of $10,000 or more: let the Investors Care Slack channel know.
Questions about the Acumatica JRE go to Alex and Macenzie. Other mail: send it in Slack directly to the person it’s for.

processes.name: Upload the annual budget into Acumatica
processes.purpose: Load the finalized budget from Budgyt into Acumatica as department budgets (Mass Budget Import), and set up the new year’s departments and P&L reports.

steps.text: Make sure no grants are blank: run a P&L in Budgyt showing only the blank grants and fix them there. Grants that are inactive in Acumatica don’t show as errors; they just don’t import.
Manual export for the GL: Periods as Columns, Exclude rows with zero, Include Grants, Summarized → Download as Importable File.
Make an Account column: just the left 4 digits.

Make a Subaccount column: the department’s 3 digits (the middle three of the file’s “Account” column), then “-”, then the 3-digit grant code (far right of the file; if a department’s account has 2 grants, pick one).
Delete the balance sheet lines and the auto lines, and change revenue to positive numbers.
Tie out: all expenses should tie to Budgyt.
Mass Budget Import → “+” → fill in the Budget Import names → upload. Check it uploaded correctly, then release. A subaccount that isn’t in Acumatica won’t import, and a notice shows on screen.
Optional: tick the checkbox when releasing the Mass Budget Import to release all its budgets automatically. That skips the approve and release steps below, and also skips reviewing them first.
Department Budget Entry: entries can’t be taken off hold in bulk, but they can be approved and released in bulk (next two steps).
“Approve Department Budgets”: every department budget with status Pending Approval.
“Release Department Budgets”: every Approved budget ready to release. Don’t release until you’re 100% confident.

sections.title: Set up the new year’s reports and departments

steps.text: Point the comparative P&L at the new budget: Finance → Column Set → DPLC Actual Budget → Data Source (bottom of the page): change columns C and G to the right “BUDGETR*”. Then Finance → Column Set → DPLM - Profit & Loss Comparative: change column C.

Add new departments: More items → Department Management → Department budget by period (pin it). Finance → Show all → Unit sets → Department → “All” → “+” to add department numbers and descriptions. In Data Source, fill “Start Sub:” and copy the same number into “End sub:”, like the others.
Create the department’s subaccounts: Departments → the department number → edit pencil by the sub segment value → select the subaccounts → Process.

Symptom: GL details for an account don’t tie to the BUDGETR amount. Check whether more than one Mass Budget Import was released for the same period: the Mass Budget Import page’s Created Budget Entries tab shows what each import created.

Reverse the extra entries. Released: click “Reverse” in the header and release the reversal entry. Approved: put it back on hold, then delete it. On hold: delete it. A Department or Grant budget that’s been completed can’t be reversed.

Payroll & 401k entries for each pay period end (the 15th and the last day of the month): review the detail of the final payroll register (department and account codes, dollar amounts, staff changes, 401k, other benefits, deductions) and make sure the balance sheet agrees. Prepared by Joel, reviewed by Macenzie.

Balance sheet review. Cash: every bank account has its final JREs (interest, gains/losses, final costs) and its bank statement is uploaded to Acumatica. Proof of Cash.

Quarterly: Overflow & National Christian Foundation. Note who prepared and who approved/released.
